RagShortTexts: The ruling elite of Hibernians comprised ancient aristocratic houses and military dynasties competing for feudal land and fiscal control.
Domestic politics were profoundly steered by court intrigues and noble factions resisting excessive central centralization.
Intricate matrimonial alliances and blood feuds permeated the nobility, ensuring that disputed successions frequently sparked nationwide crises.

Variants.Content: Within the opulent halls and sprawling feudal estates of Hibernians, the balance of domestic power remained in perilous equilibrium. Ancient lineages commanded vast agricultural latifundia, hereditary warrior retinues, and lucrative trade monopolies, acting simultaneously as imperial cornerstones and covert rivals to the throne. Court assemblies seethed with venomous factionalism, pitting entrenched senatorial aristocrats against battle-hardened military commanders who demanded greater political dominance. Behind tapestried corridors, clandestine poisonings, forged wills, and intercepted treaties dictated political ascendancy. Lesser vassals maneuvered cautiously between dominant magnates, ready to shift allegiance whenever the central authority showed signs of exhaustion or military defeat.

Two kin groups have fought over a boundary stone for a whole summer, and the chieftain's bodyguard was ordered to stand between them. A young warrior takes a spear cut he did not deserve, while the men who started the feud walk away with their pride. He spends the night cleaning his blade and wondering whose cattle the quarrel was really about.

Your foster brother is worth more than your cousin, the old chieftain tells his son, because the fosterage bond outlasts any blood feud. Keep the boundary stones where your grandfather set them, and take hostages from the families that argue. A marriage binds a border better than a sword, but only if the bride's kin keep their oaths.
